usage_note: Select a family only after current athlete/app state, active block, symptoms/function, recovery, schedule, and existing policies are applied. Exact doses remain athlete-calibrated.

recipes.title: Easy aerobic running
intended_adaptation: Aerobic consistency and low-intensity volume
Technique and impact-tolerance exposure at controllable cost
Recovery-compatible running between demanding exposures
prerequisites: No current clinical instruction that rules out running
Symptoms/function compatible with ordinary easy running
A duration or route that can be shortened without defeating the purpose
do_not_use_when: Routine optimization is inappropriate because of illness red flags, progressive function loss, or clinician restriction
The label easy would conceal a pace/terrain/heat demand that is not actually easy

preferred_intensity_anchors.anchor: heart rate below an individually credible first-threshold range

preferred_intensity_anchors.role: descriptive under comparable conditions, not a target to force

acceptable_anchor_fallbacks: Use breathing/RPE when HR, pace, terrain, or weather is unreliable
Use duration rather than distance when terrain or pace varies

illustrative_doses.example: A short-to-moderate continuous run that finishes with stable easy effort and leaves the next planned exposure feasible.
illustrative_doses.qualification: Illustrative ranges are evidence-context or coaching-convention examples, not a personalized starting prescription or universal safe dose.

illustrative_doses.example: Most annual running volume is commonly performed at low intensity, but elite frequency and volume are not portable dose recommendations.
illustrative_doses.qualification: Use only as support for easy-running predominance, not elite mileage transfer.

deliberately_athlete_calibrated: Whether frequency or duration is the next progression
progression_levers: Increase one of frequency or duration while holding intensity ordinary
Add duration to selected runs rather than every run
Choose a slightly longer known route before adding pace
regression_levers: Use flatter/softer or more familiar terrain
Substitute low-impact aerobic work if running is not tolerated
placement_constraints: Keep enough separation from quality/long-run/lower-body lifting based on actual recovery cost
Do not turn an easy day into a make-up quality session
common_execution_failures: Drifting to moderate effort because the session feels unimportant
Adding a fast finish that changes the recovery cost
modify_or_stop_signals: Worsening focal symptoms, altered gait/function, or escalating pain
Effort/breathing persistently outside intended easy domain despite slowing
Next-day delayed response materially worse than baseline
substitutions: Rest when routine training is inappropriate
monitoring: Whether the next planned session remains feasible
delayed_response: Review later-day and next-day symptoms when a run is longer, hillier, or otherwise novel
recipes.evidence_confidence: moderate for easy-running predominance; low for any exact dose

recipes.title: Long aerobic run
intended_adaptation: Durable aerobic work
Fueling and pacing practice as duration warrants
Running-specific tissue and impact tolerance
Event-relevant endurance when appropriate
prerequisites: Recent ordinary running consistency
A comparable longest recent run and known delayed response
Adequate recovery space after the session
Fueling/hydration plan when duration/conditions warrant
do_not_use_when: Delayed symptom response is deteriorating
The proposed run is a large novelty without a reason and follow-up plan
A race, quality session, or lower-body lift creates unmanageable density
The runner is returning from interruption and ordinary duration is not re-established

preferred_intensity_anchors.role: primary for ordinary long aerobic work
primary dose representation across variable pace/terrain
secondary when individual zones and sensor quality are credible

acceptable_anchor_fallbacks: Use effort and duration in heat/hills
Use a known route or out-and-back with an early turn option

illustrative_doses.example: Progress from the recent longest tolerated comparable run by changing one main lever—usually duration—then observe the delayed response before the next increase.
illustrative_doses.qualification: No universal percentage cap or weekly increase is validated.

illustrative_doses.example: Higher volume and longer endurance runs are associated with better performance, without defining an individual safe or optimal dose.
illustrative_doses.qualification: Self-selection and healthy-runner bias limit causal prescription.

progression_levers: Add a small amount of duration while keeping effort/terrain stable
Hold duration and improve execution or recovery
Add event-specific steady segments only in a later appropriate block
regression_levers: Shorten to the last tolerated duration
Split aerobic work across running and low-impact mode without calling it equivalent mileage
placement_constraints: Protect recovery before/after based on actual cost
Do not force one long run every calendar week when the rolling cadence or tolerance argues otherwise
Avoid simultaneous long-run, quality-dose, and lower-body-strength progression
common_execution_failures: Running faster because the route feels good
Using a weekly percentage cap as clearance
Ignoring delayed tenderness because the run felt fine
Making the long run the entire weekly progression
modify_or_stop_signals: Gait change or progressive focal symptoms
Effort rises beyond the intended domain
Delayed response exceeds the established baseline
substitutions: Easy run plus low-impact aerobic time on another day
Cycling/elliptical as aerobic support with no mile conversion
monitoring: Recovery time to the next planned exposure
delayed_response: Required before progression when symptoms have shown a delayed pattern
recipes.evidence_confidence: moderate for associations and rejection of universal caps; low for exact progression

recipes.title: Controlled threshold intervals
intended_adaptation: Sustainable high-aerobic/threshold-oriented work with recoveries that preserve control
Practice accumulating quality time without racing continuously
Calibrate repeatable effort and pace under standardized conditions
suitable_block_objectives: Aerobic power while mechanical risk is better controlled than in faster interval formats
prerequisites: Stable ordinary running and tolerance of some faster running
Credible effort anchor or willingness to use effort-first execution
Recovery space and compatible lower-body strength placement
do_not_use_when: The athlete is likely to race every repetition
Symptoms/function make faster running inappropriate
The current block prioritizes consistency/long-run tolerance and quality would displace it
The only anchor is a precise unverified device estimate

preferred_intensity_anchors.anchor: HR near an individually established threshold

acceptable_anchor_fallbacks: Use RPE/breathing and cap the first repetition conservatively
Use time-based repetitions on variable terrain

illustrative_doses.classification: coaching convention consistent with interval literature
illustrative_doses.example: Several controlled repetitions of roughly 3–10 minutes with easy recoveries, accumulating a modest amount of quality time while the final repeat remains technically and perceptually controlled.
illustrative_doses.qualification: Illustrative ranges are evidence-context or coaching-convention examples, not a personalized starting prescription or universal safe dose.

illustrative_doses.example: Begin with fewer/shorter repetitions or more recovery, then progress one lever only after repeat quality and delayed response are stable.
illustrative_doses.qualification: No universal initial total is established for a tendon-limited or low-volume runner.

deliberately_athlete_calibrated: Whether the workout belongs every week
progression_levers: Add one repetition
Lengthen selected work bouts
Shorten recovery modestly while retaining domain
Hold dose and improve evenness
regression_levers: Convert to steady aerobic or easy running
placement_constraints: Avoid close placement to a mechanically costly long run or interfering lower-body lift
At 3–4 runs/week, usually make this the single formal quality family rather than adding another hard session
common_execution_failures: Chasing a single target pace despite heat/hills
Interpreting completion as proof of correct threshold
modify_or_stop_signals: Unusual recovery cost that threatens the next planned exposure
substitutions: Low-impact aerobic intervals when impact is limited
delayed_response: Review before increasing total quality work or adding faster elements
recipes.evidence_confidence: moderate for controllable interval design; low for exact recreational dose

recipes.title: Continuous steady or tempo run
intended_adaptation: Sustained controlled work near a selected steady/threshold-oriented domain
Pacing discipline and continuous concentration
Event-relevant durability when appropriate
prerequisites: Reliable self-control and an effort anchor
Stable symptoms and ordinary aerobic consistency
A route/conditions where effort can be moderated
do_not_use_when: The athlete tends to turn continuous tempo into a time trial
Heat/hills make a pace target misleading and effort control is poor
Intervals would better preserve control
The session would create excessive density with long run/lifting
acceptable_anchor_fallbacks: Use progression from steady to moderately hard by effort rather than exact pace
Break into intervals when continuous control is uncertain

illustrative_doses.example: A continuous controlled segment often lies roughly in the 10–30 minute range; the correct duration is the one that preserves intended effort and recovery rather than maximizing discomfort.
illustrative_doses.qualification: Illustrative ranges are evidence-context or coaching-convention examples, not a personalized starting prescription or universal safe dose.

progression_levers: Lengthen continuous segment modestly
Hold duration and improve evenness
Use a small event-specific pace component later
regression_levers: Use steady aerobic rather than threshold-oriented effort
placement_constraints: Treat as a quality exposure even if pace is below 5K pace
Do not combine with a progressive long run unless explicitly planned and tolerated
common_execution_failures: Using current race prediction as a compulsory pace
delayed_response: Assess whether continuous load is more costly than comparable intervals
recipes.evidence_class: coaching convention supported by broader interval/threshold literature

recipes.title: Multi-minute VO2-oriented intervals
intended_adaptation: Accumulate time at high aerobic demand
Develop tolerance to fast but submaximal repeated running
Prepare for 3K–5K/mile demands when appropriate
prerequisites: Stable aerobic consistency and faster-running tolerance
Current block explicitly calls for this family
Credible effort/pace anchor and ability to avoid all-out execution
Adequate separation from long run and lower-body lifting
do_not_use_when: Current priority is rebuilding ordinary volume/tolerance
Symptoms or mechanics are unstable
The athlete cannot complete controlled repetitions without sprinting
The schedule allows no recovery margin

preferred_intensity_anchors.anchor: pace associated with recent credible 3K–5K/VO2-oriented performance

preferred_intensity_anchors.role: research concept, not a wearable target to chase

acceptable_anchor_fallbacks: Use controlled fartlek or shorter intervals by effort
Choose threshold intervals when speed/mechanical tolerance is the constraint

illustrative_doses.population: recreational and trained runners in interval studies/reviews
illustrative_doses.example: Work bouts commonly span about 2–5 minutes with easy recoveries; total fast work in research sessions varies substantially.
illustrative_doses.qualification: This describes studied formats, not a required or safe personal dose. Start from current exposure and preserve repeatability.

illustrative_doses.example: A conservative version uses fewer bouts and stops while form, effort, and pace remain repeatable; progression changes one variable.
illustrative_doses.qualification: Illustrative ranges are evidence-context or coaching-convention examples, not a personalized starting prescription or universal safe dose.

progression_levers: Add one controlled repetition
Lengthen work bouts within the same domain
Adjust recovery after stable execution
Hold dose and improve consistency
placement_constraints: Count as a major demanding exposure with substantial neuromuscular/musculoskeletal cost
Avoid novel VO2 work near progressive long runs or unfamiliar lower-body strength
Do not infer a second hard day from an 80/20 label
common_execution_failures: Maximizing total distance at vVO2max because a review reports elite examples
modify_or_stop_signals: Material rep fade despite adequate recovery
Effort becomes maximal rather than repeatable
substitutions: Low-impact high-aerobic intervals with mode-specific anchors
delayed_response: Required before increasing dose because metabolic similarity does not imply equal mechanical cost
recipes.evidence_class: review and intervention evidence with substantial protocol heterogeneity
recipes.evidence_confidence: moderate for family effects; low for exact individual format

recipes.title: Short controlled intervals or fartlek
intended_adaptation: Introduce faster aerobic running with short controllable bouts
Vary stimulus while limiting continuous strain
Develop rhythm and economy without maximal sprinting
suitable_block_objectives: Maintenance of faster running during another block
prerequisites: Stable ordinary running
Ability to keep short bouts relaxed and submaximal
Clear distinction from all-out sprint work
do_not_use_when: Short bouts encourage maximal sprinting
Mechanics/symptoms are unstable
The workout would be layered onto another quality exposure
acceptable_anchor_fallbacks: Landmark-based fartlek
Gentle pickups inside an easy run
Threshold intervals if control improves with longer bouts

illustrative_doses.example: Short-interval research spans roughly 15 seconds to under 2 minutes with many work/recovery combinations.
illustrative_doses.qualification: The literature does not establish a single best format or justify copying high session totals.

illustrative_doses.example: Use a small number of relaxed controlled pickups with generous easy running, ending before speed or form deteriorates.
illustrative_doses.qualification: Illustrative ranges are evidence-context or coaching-convention examples, not a personalized starting prescription or universal safe dose.

progression_levers: Add a small number of bouts
Lengthen bouts slightly
Reduce recovery only after control is established
regression_levers: Replace with strides or easy running
placement_constraints: Count actual intensity and mechanical novelty, not just total fast minutes
Avoid stacking with hills, strides, or plyometrics as if each were free
common_execution_failures: GPS pace chasing on short bouts
Adding more because RPE stays low early
modify_or_stop_signals: Bouts become progressively faster rather than controlled
delayed_response: Check when the session is a new speed or surface exposure
recipes.evidence_class: heterogeneous interval evidence plus coaching convention

recipes.title: Relaxed strides
intended_adaptation: Practice relaxed fast mechanics and coordination
Maintain small speed exposure without a full quality session
Prepare for later faster work when tolerated
suitable_block_objectives: Aerobic development with small speed maintenance
prerequisites: Easy running is stable
Fast running is mechanically tolerated
A safe flat surface and adequate warm-up
do_not_use_when: Symptoms worsen with faster running
The athlete interprets strides as maximal sprints
Plyometrics/hills/strength already create too much mechanical novelty

preferred_intensity_anchors.anchor: relaxed fast form with full control

acceptable_anchor_fallbacks: Gentle cadence pickups
Omit and retain easy running

illustrative_doses.classification: coaching convention; direct dose evidence insufficient
illustrative_doses.example: Several short accelerations commonly around 10–25 seconds with full easy recovery, stopping well before all-out sprinting.
illustrative_doses.qualification: Illustrative ranges are evidence-context or coaching-convention examples, not a personalized starting prescription or universal safe dose.

progression_levers: Improve relaxation at the same dose
Add one or two repetitions
Slightly lengthen only while remaining nonmaximal
placement_constraints: Place after an easy warm-up/run when symptoms and coordination are normal
Count as mechanical fast exposure around lifting/hills
common_execution_failures: Using strides to rescue a missed quality session
substitutions: Controlled short hills only if hill tolerance is better established
monitoring: Interaction with strength and next quality session
delayed_response: Review next day when speed exposure is new or tendon symptoms are relevant

recipes.title: Controlled hills or short fast uphill work
intended_adaptation: Running-specific strength/economy and controlled fast mechanics
Introduce intensity with terrain-mediated speed
Race-specific hill skill when relevant
prerequisites: Stable symptoms and ordinary running
Known tolerance to grade/surface
Clear hill type: short fast versus longer aerobic/threshold hill
do_not_use_when: Posterior-chain/calf/tendon loading is not tolerated
The route forces aggressive downhill recovery
The session duplicates plyometric or lower-body strength stress
The athlete will sprint maximally
acceptable_anchor_fallbacks: Gentle rolling route at easy effort
Flat strides
Omit fast component

illustrative_doses.example: Short controlled uphill repetitions often last roughly 8–20 seconds with full walk/jog recovery; longer 30–120-second hills are a different, more metabolically demanding session family.
illustrative_doses.qualification: Illustrative ranges are evidence-context or coaching-convention examples, not a personalized starting prescription or universal safe dose.

progression_levers: Improve form at same dose
Add one repetition
Lengthen only if session purpose changes deliberately
regression_levers: Use flat relaxed strides or easy running
placement_constraints: Treat short fast hills as mechanical quality
Avoid near unfamiliar calf/leg strength or plyometrics
Account for downhill eccentric cost
common_execution_failures: Combining short sprints and longer hill intervals unintentionally
delayed_response: Explicit next-day check when hills are novel or tendon symptoms have delayed behavior

recipes.title: Controlled benchmark or race-specific session
intended_adaptation: Answer a defined performance/calibration question
Practice event rhythm, pacing, and decision making
Provide a transition signal when evidence is credible
prerequisites: A written decision question
Known event/benchmark protocol and conditions
Sufficient recovery and mechanical readiness
A plan for interpreting ambiguous results
do_not_use_when: The only purpose is to prove fitness
A maximal test would disrupt the more important training sequence
Conditions are too incomparable for the decision
Symptoms/illness make maximal or specific work inappropriate
acceptable_anchor_fallbacks: Standardized submaximal comparison
Controlled workout rather than maximal test
Defer test and use broader effort anchors

illustrative_doses.classification: decision framework, not a fixed dose
illustrative_doses.example: Select the least costly repeatable protocol that can resolve the decision; maximal races/time trials are optional, not default.
illustrative_doses.qualification: Standardization and repeatability matter more than a universal distance.

illustrative_doses.example: Use controlled segments at event-relevant rhythm only after prerequisites; keep total dose familiar enough that it informs rather than derails the block.
illustrative_doses.qualification: Illustrative ranges are evidence-context or coaching-convention examples, not a personalized starting prescription or universal safe dose.

progression_levers: Increase specificity before total stress
Lengthen race-specific segments while reducing unrelated load
Use a more demanding benchmark only when it changes a decision
placement_constraints: Replace another demanding exposure; do not simply add it
Allow recovery and taper context appropriate to priority
Avoid novel shoes/surface/fueling when measurement is the goal
common_execution_failures: Recalibrating every zone from one result
Treating a good result as clearance for simultaneous progressions
monitoring: Decision made from result and confidence
delayed_response: Include event/benchmark recovery and later symptoms before block transition
recipes.evidence_confidence: moderate for standardization principles; low for universal test choice

recipes.title: Low-impact aerobic substitution
intended_adaptation: Maintain or supplement cardiorespiratory work when impact load is constrained
Preserve routine while running-specific tolerance is rebuilt
Provide a lower-impact option after schedule or symptom modification
suitable_block_objectives: Volume support without claiming running equivalence
prerequisites: Chosen mode is itself tolerated
Mode-specific intensity anchor
Clear reason for substitution or addition
No clinical instruction against exercise
do_not_use_when: The mode aggravates symptoms
It is used to hide an unresolved running/clinical problem
Minutes are converted automatically to running miles
It creates extra fatigue that undermines running or strength priorities
acceptable_anchor_fallbacks: Easy conversational mode without exact metrics
Rest if ordinary aerobic work is inappropriate

illustrative_doses.population: runners using cycling or other aerobic modes
illustrative_doses.example: Small studies and meta-analyses support preservation of some aerobic fitness with cross-training, but protocols vary and do not establish one-for-one running equivalence.
illustrative_doses.qualification: Set duration and effort from the chosen mode, recovery cost, and current objective.

progression_levers: Increase mode-specific duration modestly
Add controlled intervals only when appropriate
Improve consistency without displacing key running
placement_constraints: Track as its own mode and load
Do not assume low impact means zero recovery cost
Coordinate with lower-body strength and next run
common_execution_failures: Turning every substitute into a hard session
Adding rather than replacing after a missed run
modify_or_stop_signals: Next key running or strength session becomes compromised
substitutions: Elliptical/pool running if tolerated and available
delayed_response: Review symptoms and next-run tolerance; aerobic maintenance does not prove impact tolerance
recipes.evidence_confidence: low-moderate for aerobic support; low for equivalence
